rationale: As a contact sheet, this reads as only about five visible families, with a dominant compact box/slab language occupying roughly half the set. The portfolio is therefore not yet diverse enough for a 20-option hard pass, and the repeated open-court / entry-notch / stepped-box themes make the sheet feel redundant. The better options are those where void, threshold, and section are clearly spatial rather than decorative; the weaker ones are generic bars or boxes with minor cuts. The next batch should intentionally diversify footprint and section relationships while preserving the required active street edge and a usable public void or terrace.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: single-bar / slab-like box with open-court subtraction and stepped top; same footprint logic recurs with minor roof variations
compact stepped block with front-access notch/cut and similar stacked massing
compact box with one-sided entry carve / appendage and minimal sectional differentiation

required_next_relations: Introduce at least 2-3 new families beyond bar/block: bent-bar courtyard, split-wing bridge, cross-mass with central void, cantilever over active ground edge, cut-corner terrace, or attached volume with a true threshold gap.

Vary section depth and roof logic together: one family should be low-and-wide with a voided court, another should be lifted to create a sheltered street porch, another should step back to form a usable terrace.
Keep the west street edge legible and programmatic in every new family: retail/cafe/community entry should occupy the active ground threshold rather than disappearing into a generic box.
Avoid repeating the same simple box chassis with different labels; change footprint, section, and void location simultaneously so the family reads as materially different at thumbnail scale.
Ensure at least three options show explicit courtyard/cut/notch relations tied to mixed-use ground space and not just cosmetic subtraction.
